disposition_mapping.rationale: Manual checklist distribution and cutoff confirmation are restructured into continuous, system-enforced cutoff monitoring and automated task distribution, preserving the period-cutoff discipline required by IAS 1 (KB-03).

The mixed mechanical/judgmental nature of journal preparation is split: template-driven accruals and prepayment releases are automated with exception review (TS-02), while estimation entries requiring documented judgment (provisions, ECL, NRV write-downs) remain a distinct human-performed step (TS-03), preserving the accrual mechanism (KB-01), estimate documentation (KB-04, KB-10) and error-correction path (KB-05).

Allocation processing is restructured into a system-driven automated allocation run with exception-based human validation of allocation bases, retaining the same functional outcome with reduced manual effort.

Intercompany processing survives as required (R2R-R-02): high-volume matching is automated while inter-entity mismatch resolution, settlement and elimination-entry preparation remain human-performed, preserving the completeness of intragroup identification and elimination required by IFRS 10 (KB-14).

GL reconciliation survives as required (R2R-R-01), restructured into a risk-based model where automated matching handles low-risk volume and human certification concentrates on high-risk and exception items, preserving the evidential trail required by IAS 1 (KB-02) and error-correction (KB-05).

Consolidation is restructured around an automated consolidation engine but retains mandatory FX retranslation (KB-07), exchange-difference tracking (KB-08) and policy-consistent computation (KB-06) as non-negotiable accounting computations.

Management review survives as required (R2R-R-07), retained substantially unchanged and performed by the controller, distinct from journal-preparing actors (R2R-R-05), preserving faithful representation (KB-02).

The reporting package function survives as required (R2R-R-06), retained with automated compilation, and remains ordered after both reconciliation (TS-06) and management review (TS-08) per R2R-R-03 and R2R-R-04.

steps.description: Maintain a continuous close calendar with automated subledger cutoff monitoring (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll); system-enforced posting locks triggered at defined cutoff times; automated distribution of task assignments and deadlines via a workflow platform; real-time dashboard of data readiness replaces manual checklist distribution while preserving period-cutoff discipline.
inputs: Subledger status feeds (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll)
steps.name: Continuous close orchestration and cutoff control
outputs: Data readiness monitored in real time

steps.description: System auto-generates recurring accrual and prepayment-release journals from templates and amortisation schedules, and applies rule-based reclassification/error-correction entries; GL accountant reviews only system-flagged exceptions and approves auto-posted mechanical entries by exception, preserving the accrual mechanism and error-correction path.
steps.name: Automated recurring journal generation

steps.description: Prepare provisions and estimates requiring judgment and a documented basis (bad debt/expected credit loss, inventory net realisable value write-downs, litigation), with supporting evidence retained and reviewed against prior-period basis for policy consistency; post estimation journals with full audit trail.
steps.name: Estimation and judgmental provisioning
outputs: Estimation journals posted with documented basis and evidence

steps.description: Run system-driven cost and overhead allocations per the allocation model (shared-service recharges, corporate overhead distribution, intercompany management fees); automated validation of allocation bases against cost-centre data with exception-based human review of variances before posting.
steps.name: Automated cost and overhead allocations

steps.description: High-volume, rule-based automated matching of intercompany balances (AR/AP mirror accounts, loans, recharges) across entities; system flags mismatches for investigation; intercompany accountant coordinates with counterparty entities to resolve exceptions, processes settlements/netting, and prepares elimination entries ensuring intragroup positions are fully identifiable and eliminable.
steps.name: Automated intercompany matching and exception resolution

steps.description: Automated system matching reconciles GL to subledgers, bank statements and supporting schedules for low-risk, high-volume accounts; risk-rated accounts determine reconciliation frequency and reviewer requirements; GL accountant certifies reconciliations with supporting evidence, concentrating effort on exception-based and high-risk items; unreconciled items are flagged and aged for resolution.
steps.name: Risk-based GL and balance-sheet reconciliation

steps.description: Prepare the trial balance; run an automated consolidation engine across entities including currency retranslation at closing rates, elimination of intercompany balances and unrealised profit using the elimination entries from intercompany processing, and minority-interest processing; validate consolidated balances against entity submissions and track exchange differences explicitly.
steps.name: Trial balance, consolidation, FX translation and eliminations

steps.description: Review draft consolidated results against expectations and prior period using analytics-driven variance flagging; investigate anomalies; determine, document and post management adjustments; sign off account-level results for reporting. Performed by the controller, independent of the accountants who prepared the underlying journals, preserving segregation of duties.
steps.name: Management review and adjustments

steps.description: Compile the period-end reporting package (financial statements, management commentary, variance schedules, KPI summaries) using automated report generation from signed-off consolidated results; distribute to management and group per the reporting timetable.
steps.name: Financial reporting package
